signet_channel.note: Reuploads of the artists' published clips with their explicit permission (Daniel, 2026-09-06). NO CREDIT LINE IN THE DESCRIPTIONS. They carried 'Filmed and first published by [artist]; reuploaded with permission.' for one day; Daniel killed it 2026-09-06 and it was stripped from all 24 live descriptions the same evening. His words: 'it makes me look like an unaffiliated leach. i have full permission for all of this.' These are the roster, and a repost disclaimer on a Signet artist's video frames the company as a stranger who found the clip rather than the agency that books the act. The permission is recorded here and in site-ops/FOOTAGE-TITLES.md, which is where it belongs; it is not announced to the public. Same rule the photographs already followed (img/SOURCES.md). Do not reinstate it. Site embeds point at the Signet copy once it exists; the original ID stays here as provenance.

BOTH HALVES ARE DONE, except for two videos that are not his to give. Site: nine photographs and six embeds, live. YouTube: the four cuts on his own channel were reuploaded to @SignetArtists the same evening with the footage/reuploads pipeline (Entuned OAuth client, yt_upload.py), keys 21 to 24, and the page embeds the Signet copies. The Thrill Is Gone published as a Short: vertical and under three minutes. All four verified public and embeddable before the embeds were swapped, and added to the channel playlists including a new 'Tony Medina, blues and rock'. HERO SWAPPED the same evening to mHtY8DbqLtA (the Signet copy of his Prince cover), so nothing at the top of the page depends on a third-party channel. STILL OPEN: t_s2FavrDew ('Going Down', now a footage tile) and qf4_7lKu3iE ('Don't Drink The Water') sit on the SIDEHATCH ARTS channel, not on Tony's. His permission covers his material, not another channel's upload, so those two still embed the original and need SIDEHATCH's word before a Signet copy goes up. Tracked in Asana.
